hero_kpi_rationale: Collectibles revenue is a key segment of the business, growing 47.7% in 2025 and now representing 29.2% of total net sales, up from 18.8% the prior year. This rapid expansion illustrates GameStop's strategic transformation beyond traditional video game retail.

kpis.name: Collectibles Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from the sale of collectibles (trading cards, figurines, collectible items)
kpis.description: Collectibles revenue increased 47.7% in 2025, rising from $717.9M to $1,060.2M, representing 29.2% of total net sales (versus 18.8% the prior year).

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of net sales remaining after deducting cost of goods sold (COGS)
kpis.description: Gross margin improved by 390 basis points in 2025, increasing from 29.1% to 33.0%, primarily driven by a favorable product mix (higher-margin collectibles growth).

kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.description: Net sales declined 5.1% in 2025, decreasing from $3,823.0M to $3,629.9M, primarily due to lower software sales (-27.5%) and hardware sales (-12.3%), partially offset by collectibles growth.

kpis.name: Operating Income
kpis.explanation: Operating profit after deduction of operating expenses
kpis.description: Operating income improved from a loss of $26.2M in 2024 to a profit of $232.1M in 2025 (6.4% of net sales), driven by gross margin expansion and a $220.2M reduction in SG&A expenses.

kpis.name: Net Interest Income
kpis.explanation: Net interest income generated from cash and investments
kpis.description: Net interest income increased 66.2% in 2025, rising from $163.4M to $271.5M, driven by proceeds from convertible note issuances and active cash management.

kpis.name: Collectibles Revenue Growth
kpis.explanation: Growth rate of collectibles revenue, illustrating the business model transformation
kpis.description: Collectibles revenue increased 47.7% in 2025, rising from $717.9M to $1,060.2M. This category now represents 29.2% of total net sales, up from 18.8% in 2024, reflecting the company's diversification strategy beyond traditional video games.

risks.title: Stock price volatility
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions extreme volatility in GME's stock price, citing the 2021 short squeeze as a major example. This volatility is deemed disproportionate to operational performance, indicating a significant risk to shareholders. The 'Capital' category is weighted as it directly affects valuation and market perception.

risks.title: Dependence on video game and hardware sales
risks.score_rationale: Data shows significant declines in 'Hardware and accessories' (-12.3%) and 'Software' (-27.5%) sales in 2025. While 'Collectibles' are growing, the sharp decline in traditional categories indicates a dependence that poses a risk if these markets continue to weaken. The 'Industrial' category is relevant as it pertains to the core product sales business.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and data protection risks
risks.score_rationale: Although the document details governance measures and a dedicated cybersecurity team, the mere emphasis on the importance of these controls and the reference to Item 1A for further details ('for additional information about the risks to our business associated with a breach or compromise to our data and information security systems') suggest a material risk. The 'Cybersecurity' category is high-priority for any technology-facing company.

risks.title: Optimization and restructuring of international operations
risks.score_rationale: The text mentions divestitures in Canada and New Zealand, as well as closures in Germany and Italy. These restructurings resulted in significant asset impairments and reduced sales in certain regions. The 'Macro' category applies as it encompasses strategic geographic expansion/contraction decisions.

risks.title: Lease and retail location management
risks.score_rationale: The document details the upcoming expiration of leases for numerous stores and distribution centers in the coming years. While the company expresses confidence in renewals or relocations, poor management of these expirations could lead to unexpected costs or operational disruptions. The 'Industrial' category applies to commercial real estate and operational logistics.

risks.title: Risk related to digital assets and cryptocurrencies
risks.score_rationale: The report notes a significant loss related to digital assets and associated receivables ('Loss on digital assets and related receivables' of $131.6 million). This indicates exposure to the volatility and inherent risks of this market. The 'Technology' category is relevant for digital asset exposure.

ai_positioning.summary: GME does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
